title: Punt 3PTM: Player Targets
brief: Which players fit a punt 3PTM build in our league, grouped into tiers with what each adds in FG%, REB and BLK? It must note that threes are easy to find on waivers, so non-shooters lose less than rankings suggest.
summary: Punting 3PTM costs little in our league. Threes are easy to stream off waivers, and about two threes a game is now only average, so non-shooters lose less than their rankings suggest. Build around Amen Thompson, Jalen Duren and Dyson Daniels. Add 8 to 14 USD centers for FG%, REB and BLK, then fill the end of the auction with 1 to 5 USD bigs.

sections.heading: Why non-shooters lose less than rankings suggest

paragraphs.text: Threes are the easiest category to find on waivers. Three-point specialists show up there all season, so do not pay auction money for them. Overall rankings count a player's missing threes as a full loss. In our league you can replace that production with a free pickup, so the real loss is smaller.

The bar for threes has also gone up. About two threes a game is now average in fantasy. A shooter who makes only two a game is nothing special, and the same raw volume is worth less than it used to be. Do not spend mid-auction money on a player whose main selling point is two threes a game.

What to do in season: we get 6 acquisitions per week. If a matchup is close in 3PTM late in the week, spend one or two of them on a waiver shooter. Do not draft for threes. Save the auction money for FG%, REB and BLK.

Threes and FG% pull against each other. When you drop threes, your FG% goes up. Rebounds, blocks and FG% move together, so most punt 3PTM targets are centers and athletic wings who score near the rim. FG% is a team ratio. High-volume finishers like Duren and Zion move it most. Low-volume players like Queta, Murray-Boyles and McConnell move it less than their percentages suggest.

The risk is that the build gets too narrow. Only REB, BLK and FG% move together naturally, which makes a pure big man build harder to run. Fix this by spending your top dollars on non-shooters who also bring guard stats. Amen Thompson adds steals. Daniels adds steals and assists. Ausar Thompson adds steals. Hartenstein adds assists from the center spot.

Watch FT% as you build. Duren's FT% does not hurt much, and Zubac takes only 2.8 FT attempts a game. Gobert, Ausar Thompson, Zion and Claxton do hurt FT%. If you roster two or more of them, you are also close to punting FT%, so decide that on purpose.

Early stage: get one or two core pieces. Amen Thompson is fair up to the high 30s. Duren's stop point is 20 to 24 USD. Daniels is worth 18 to 24 USD. These three give the most FG%, REB, steals and blocks per dollar among non-shooters.

Middle stage: add centers at capped prices. Pay about 13 to 14 USD for Allen, 10 to 14 USD for Zubac, 8 to 12 USD for Gobert, about 11 USD for Edey and 14 to 18 USD for Ausar Thompson. Do not go above 10 USD for Zion. Our league overpaid for several of these players last season, so ignore last year's prices.

Late stage: fill the last spots with 1 to 5 USD bigs. Good options are Queta, Hartenstein, Poeltl, Claxton, Gafford, Missi, Diabaté, Isaiah Jackson and Murray-Boyles. A 1 USD IL stash such as Butler or Konan Niederhäuser only makes sense if you have a free IL slot. Players ranked well past 144 should stay on waivers. Mitchell Robinson, Lively, Ayton and Beringer are examples.

Check playoff schedules before you pay. Houston has only 10 games in our playoff weeks. Indiana plays 3, 4 and 3 games. Minnesota has a two-game semifinal week. Dallas plays 4, 4 and 4, and the Clippers play 4, 3 and 4, which helps Lively and Konan Niederhäuser late in the season.

There are three price splits. On Amen Thompson, the experts value him at 35 to 40 USD, but Lloyd calls him a third-round pick at about 28 to 30 USD if his blocks and FG% do not come back. On Edey, he went for 20 USD in a mock, while Josh capped him at 11 USD because of his foot and ankle risk. On Duren, ESPN's value is 34 USD, but a mock auction gave him 19 USD. Our rule: bid to the lower number unless early news supports the higher one.

The method notes also pull in two directions. One view says non-shooters are barely hurt because threes are easy to stream. The other says the big man build is hard to run because only REB, BLK and FG% move together. Both can hold at once. Punting threes is cheap, but your roster still needs steals and assists from somewhere.

sections.heading: What to check in the first weeks

paragraphs.text: Minutes decide most of these players. Check whether Duren gets above 28 minutes and Allen gets close to 30. Check that Queta starts over Mitchell Robinson, Missi starts over Queen, and Diabaté holds about 26 minutes. Check whether Amen Thompson's blocks get back near 0.9 and his FG% gets near 55%.

Some backups are injury handcuffs. Add them with FAB as soon as the starter ahead of them misses games: Paul Reed for Duren, Beringer for Gobert, Ayton for Anthony Davis, and Kalkbrenner if Diabaté or another Charlotte big gets hurt.
